rfm_tuples.M_value: Al Shimari judgment: 3 plaintiffs × ($3M compensatory + $11M punitive) = $42M total. Doe decision on Alien Tort Statute scope). NO loss accrual recorded. The Abbass companion case has 46 plaintiffs with identical allegations; the District Court has said it will NOT reactivate Abbass while Al Shimari is on appeal. If SCOTUS denies cert or upholds, the Abbass exposure is approximately 46/3 × $42M = ~$640M of compensatory + punitive equivalent at the Al Shimari per-plaintiff rate. EDGAR FTS: 10 Abu Ghraib hits and 23 Al Shimari hits — disclosure cadence is appropriate. Critical Mode-B observation: CACI's General Counsel Koegel sold $1.23M @ $615.06 on FEBRUARY 10, 2026 — only 31 days before the Court of Appeals affirmation against the Company that was oral-argued back in September 2025. rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the most material risk-factor in the file. The 2-1 affirmation creates a likely-payable $42M judgment (CACI must post a supersedeas bond if it wants to stay execution pending SCOTUS, typically 110-120% of the judgment = $46-50M cash). More importantly, the Abbass case becomes immediately re-activatable once Al Shimari is final — and 46 plaintiffs at the Al Shimari per-plaintiff rate = ~$640M of contingent liability. The 10-K and Q3 10-Q recording ZERO accrual is defensible under ASC 450 ('probable AND estimable') only if rehearing/SCOTUS reversal is more-likely-than-not, but a 2-1 appellate affirmation makes that posture difficult to sustain. The Koegel + Plunkett discretionary sales in the 30 days before the ruling are a Mode-B governance flag the framework picks up. Severe-underdelivery on disclosure-vs-management-action coherence; partially mitigated by the disclosure itself being detailed and the legal arguments (state secrets, derivative sovereign immunity) being substantive.

summary: CACI is a MEDIUM-CONVICTION LONG with mixed signals. The OPERATIONAL thesis is intact: FY25 revenue $8.63B +12.6% YoY (7.2% organic), Q3 FY26 organic growth ACCELERATED to 6.8% in a sector procurement slowdown (USAspending confirms award count -32% YoY but dollar volume only -7%, the BAH-mirror pattern), backlog +6.4% YoY to $33.4B with funded backlog +19% to $5.0B — CACI is OUTPERFORMING the BAH/peer slowdown narrative. ARKA Group acquisition (Mar 9, 2026, $1.275B EV from Blackstone) is a strategic capability fill for Golden Dome/OBBBA $25B space funding, financed at-market with NO yield concession (Additional 6.375% Senior Notes 2033, Term Loan B-2 at SOFR+margin). Board refresh in Dec 2025 added former Navy CNO Michael Gilday + former NOC CFO David Keffer — best-in-cohort governance upgrade pre-acquisition. Five-year cleanness scan is exemplary: ZERO qui tam, ZERO civil investigative demand, ZERO Item 4.02 restatement, ZERO material weakness, ZERO going-concern. Auditor PwC (3-year tenure post-rotation from EY 2022). IRS audit FY17-21 concluded clean in FY25 (benefited tax rate). Operating cash flow $547M FY25 (110% of net income), 9MFY26 +$117M YoY further boosted by OBBBA R&D deduction restoration. HOWEVER, the LONG thesis is materially WEAKENED by two findings: (1) ZERO insider open-market PURCHASES across the 3.5-year window (vs BAH CEO Rozanski's $2M buy 6 days after the slowdown 8-K); post-drawdown insider SALES total $8.13M ALL DISCRETIONARY (not 10b5-1) — including CEO Mengucci's $5.01M sale Sep 15 2025 (5 weeks post-10K), Director Jews's $1.76M sale Dec 10 then resignation Dec 24, GC Koegel's $1.23M sale Feb 10 (31 days pre-Abu Ghraib appellate loss), and Director Plunkett's $0.13M sale Mar 11 (ONE DAY pre-public ruling). (2) The Mar 12 2026 Fourth Circuit AFFIRMED the $42M Al Shimari Abu Ghraib judgment 2-1; CACI has recorded ZERO loss accrual and is petitioning for rehearing/SCOTUS. The Abbass companion case has 46 plaintiffs at identical exposure rate = ~$644M implied tail liability if Al Shimari fails at SCOTUS. Buyback paused at zero in 9MFY26 (vs BAH which accelerated buybacks) — capital redirected to ARKA. Leverage steps up from 3.12x to ~4.24x pro-forma. Net: structural business is HIGH quality (backlog, organic growth, cleared workforce moat, board refresh, cash flow) but management capital-allocation choices (no buyback into 24% drawdown + zero P-buys + discretionary sales by GC/directors in the 30 days pre-Abu Ghraib ruling) reduce the conviction to MED. LONG-tier with caution flag — recommend smaller position size than BAH.
